drhp.business: The company delivers signalling, electrification, track and systems-integration projects across India for Indian Railways, metro corporations and private industrial clients, executing through two verticals: B2G (direct Indian Railways, PSUs and Metros) and B2B (private railway sidings, upgradation/modernisation and composite maintenance projects). Its deep-tech subsidiary NOVA Control Technologix is developing indigenous SIL-4 safety-critical products, including Kavach Automatic Train Protection, alongside an in-house Engineering Design & Research Centre (EDRC) that covers pre-bid engineering, detailed design, verification & validation, execution support and commissioning.
drhp.co: E TO E TRANS INFRA LTD
drhp.end_markets: Indian Railways|PSUs|Metro rail networks|Private and industrial rail sidings|International markets (14 countries)
drhp.expansion: NOVA Control Tecnologix's engineering and manufacturing facility for safety-critical rail products was inaugurated and the product platform launched on 23 October 2025 in Bengaluru, marking the company's transition from a systems integrator to an OEM. Through FY26, NOVA built the vital-card family, a three-domain safety software platform and an in-house Network Management System. NOVA is co-developing KAVACH 4.0, an Automatic Train Protection system built to SIL-4 discipline, jointly with Tata Elxsi, with manufacturing of vital cards/PCB assembly split as NOVA design / Syrma build. The company's strategic direction going forward is to certify and deploy KAVACH 4.0, then scale the installed base across Indian Railways, and ultimately establish India/NOVA as an export hub for railway safety technology.
drhp.mdna: Indian Railways is entering a significant cycle of signalling and train-control system modernisation, driven by the need to enhance safety, increase network capacity, improve operating speeds and efficiency, and prepare the network for future economic requirements.|Programmes such as Kavach, signalling modernisation and broader adoption of next-generation train-control technologies are creating opportunities of considerable scale.|Management expects growth to increasingly come from product-led businesses rather than only systems-integration execution.|The combination of established project execution capabilities, a growing order pipeline and NOVA's emerging product/technology portfolio is positioned to let the company participate in the railway-modernisation transformation.|Order book crossed the ₹1,000 crore level in June 2026, providing revenue visibility and marking a milestone in the company's evolution.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian Railways is entering a significant cycle of signalling and train-control system modernisation, driven by the need to enhance safety, increase network capacity, improve operating speeds and efficiency, and prepare the network for future economic requirements.
- Programmes such as Kavach, signalling modernisation and broader adoption of next-generation train-control technologies are creating opportunities of considerable scale.
- Management expects growth to increasingly come from product-led businesses rather than only systems-integration execution.
- The combination of established project execution capabilities, a growing order pipeline and NOVA's emerging product/technology portfolio is positioned to let the company participate in the railway-modernisation transformation.
- Order book crossed the ₹1,000 crore level in June 2026, providing revenue visibility and marking a milestone in the company's evolution.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: NOVA Control Tecnologix's engineering and manufacturing facility for safety-critical rail products was inaugurated and the product platform launched on 23 October 2025 in Bengaluru, marking the company's transition from a systems integrator to an OEM. Through FY26, NOVA built the vital-card family, a three-domain safety software platform and an in-house Network Management System. NOVA is co-developing KAVACH 4.0, an Automatic Train Protection system built to SIL-4 discipline, jointly with Tata Elxsi, with manufacturing of vital cards/PCB assembly split as NOVA design / Syrma build. The company's strategic direction going forward is to certify and deploy KAVACH 4.0, then scale the installed base across Indian Railways, and ultimately establish India/NOVA as an export hub for railway safety technology.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- technology: 100% indigenous design for NOVA's safety-critical products, with no foreign licence, no royalty and sovereign patching rights — evidence: "100% indigenous design — no foreign licence, no royalty, sovereign patching rights"
- licence/regulatory: received CCA approval from RDSO unlocking access to Kavach field-trial orders — evidence: "The Company has received CCA approval from RDSO, which enables it to obtain field trial orders for Kavach development"
- technology: NOVA RAKSHA is a single SIL-4 certified compute core from which eleven products are derived, giving platform leverage across the product range — evidence: "NOVA RAKSHA — one SIL-4 certified compute core, eleven products derived from it"
- integration: full-stack coverage from design through O&M gives single-point accountability across critical railway interfaces — evidence: "Integrated capabilities across design → engineering → execution → commissioning → O&M → products. Single-point accountability across critical railway interfaces."
- distribution: established execution footprint across a large, diversified client base and network length — evidence: "65+ clients
- 160+ projects
- 14 countries
- 2,500+ km network footprint" — against it: B2B vertical carries high working-capital needs from long receivable cycles (DSO >120 days)

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company discloses 'power of buyers' as HIGH: 'Indian Railways and a small set of metro corporations account for most demand. Specifications standardised, tendering price-led.'
- Barriers to entry the company itself must also clear: 'Multi-year SIL-4 campaigns, RDSO type approval, scarce field-trial slots, and working capital that must survive a long public procurement cycle.'
- Company discloses 'power of suppliers' as MEDIUM: 'Concentrated in safety processor SoCs, FPGAs and the certified safe RTOS — c.12-15% of hardware BOM value.'
- Company discloses competitive rivalry as MED-HIGH, naming 'Global: Siemens, Alstom, Thales, Hitachi, Wabtec, Knorr-Bremse, Frauscher. Domestic: Medha, HBL, Kernex, Quadrant, CRIS.'

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to invest in R&D and engineering, and build and commercialise differentiated products.
- Expand the multi-product platform, with interoperability at its core, rather than isolated products.
- Deepen participation in India's railway modernisation while increasingly looking beyond India for global mobility-market opportunities.
- Transition from systems-integration execution capability to technology ownership through NOVA, developing and owning indigenous safety-critical railway technologies.
- Progress NOVA RAKSHA as a safety-critical technology platform intended to become the foundation for a suite of next-generation signalling, train-control and locomotive products.
- Build alongside the railway ecosystem (administrations, operators, technology companies, system integrators) rather than outside it, including collaborative development such as with Tata Elxsi on Kavach 4.0.
- Strengthen institutional governance, compliance, financial controls, risk management and quality systems as the company scales as a listed entity.
